sections.hypothesis: Among liquid coins with a USDT-M perpetual, those whose perp funding was lowest over the past week (least crowded long) beat the average coin over the next week in spot, beyond their own past week and size, by more than a weekly round trip.
sections.rationale: Who pays: positive funding is longs paying shorts to keep leveraged long positions open, so high funding marks crowded, expensive positioning; when it unwinds, the crowded coins fall hardest, and the uncrowded ones don't carry that overhang. Kestrel can't take the short side (spot, long-only, P5 parked), so the usable form is choosing which coins to hold. Outside evidence, unverified: an outside AI review (2026-11-16) cited 'Anatomy of Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures Returns' (2024) on basis and funding as predictors of futures returns, and a 2026 blog reporting a modest funding cross-section after costs; neither has been read here, so they are leads, not evidence. Kestrel's own funding tests were different and failed: a crowding filter on holding BTC and ETH, and on trend-vol-target, both in time (one coin, in or out), not across coins. This is a new question: relative, across many coins, weekly. Funding data: Binance's archive for the 144 study coins with a perp (fetched 2026-11-16 before this note's run; nothing computed on it).
sections.rules: kestrel cross-study funding --research <this note>. Signal: minus the mean funding rate of the coin's USDT-M perpetual (XUSDT, or 1000XUSDT) over settlements in the 7 days strictly before the Sunday close; coins with no perp or no settlements carry no signal that week. Universe: the exploration half of research/exploration/split.toml plus BTC, ETH and SOL (the locked confirmation half is never read). Daily bars before 2025-11-01. Each Sunday close (the bar opening Sunday 00:00 UTC), a coin is eligible with 180+ days of history and a 30-day median daily quote volume of 20M USDT or more. Next week: log return from that close to the close 7 days later (a missing bar leaves that coin-week out). Controls: the past week's log return and log of the 30-day median volume. Each week with 10+ eligible coins carrying the signal: next-week returns regressed on the z-scored signal, past week and size; the signal's coefficient averaged over weeks (Fama-MacBeth), P(mean > 0) by 5,000 bootstrap resamples of weeks (seed 0). Long-only: each week the top fifth of coins by signal against the average eligible coin.
sections.falsification: PROCEED to a strategy note only if the signal's mean coefficient is positive with P(> 0) of at least 90%, AND the top fifth beats the average eligible coin by more than one weekly round trip: 2 x (7.5 bps fee + 8 bps half-spread, the 20M-100M band) = 0.31% a week. Otherwise KILL. Run once. The overlap with the past week's return is reported whatever the verdict.
sections.parameters: 7-day funding window, Sunday closes, the eligibility rule above, fifths, 5,000 resamples: fixed before the run. No other window or cut is tried.
sections.costs: Weekly rebalancing of a few coins: one round trip a week is the hurdle above. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.
